title: Charles III of Lorraine to the count of Vaudémont, copy
correspondents: Charles III, duke of Lorraine → François, comte de Vaudémont
shelfmark: BnF fr. 3621 no. 97 (fol. 109); no. 22 (fol. 31) is the January decipherment
folio_note: canvas = 2 x folio + 9; no. 97 at fol. 109 = canvas 227, no. 22 at fol. 31 = canvas 71; the folio printed before a piece number belongs to it
status: Attempted 18 Sept 2026 (targets/lorraine1592/, PR #4): the reciprocal letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (Tomokiyo had broken it in 2025 without publishing a text); no. 22 is a plaintext decipherment of the January letter, with no cipher. Removed from the catalogue when first claimed solved; restored 23 Oct 2026: Reading audit 22-23 Oct 2026 (George Lasry's test: a reading must build sentences): no. 97 decodes into fragments with a gap in almost every line, so nothing counts as read.
why: Lorraine's double game between the League and Henri IV. The ciphered passages carry the military business the clear text only skirts: prisoners and munitions, an order to receive the Duke's commandment and to conserve the plain, Chasteauvillain, and the intention to bring the army back into the quarters of La Fauche, between Neufchateau and Chaumont. The clear text around them has the attempt on Chasteauvillain, munitions promised and undelivered, Chaumont and Buzonville; no. 22's decipherment carries the January business - the Spanish march on Rouen, Mayenne finding the Spaniards resolved on battle, Parma's judgement, then the legate, the Spanish pretensions, Villeroy at Pontoise, the house of Bourbon, Bellievre, and the peace.
known: Letter-pair key recovered from the ciphertext alone (lorraine1592.html).
open: Special signs inside words (about 60 tokens), figures 57, 98, 122, 123, 13, 137, 88, 146, 121, 103, garbled runs L12, L13, L20; no sentence builds. Blocker: no key material; a key or duplicate may survive in the Lorraine ducal archive (AD Meurthe-et-Moselle).

status: Narrowed 20 Oct 2026 to the two Sega items. The Baudouin-Desportes letters (fr. 3984 f. 186, f. 189) were deciphered by Paolo Rosson on 1 Oct 2026 with Tomokiyo's League key, checked here and written up (targets/desportes1593/, desportes1593.html). Open: no. 8 is a homophonic substitution with a small nomenclator (Z separates words; D, N, X nulls), no. 6 continuous figures (3 and 8 nulls, letters as figure pairs, codes framed by nulls), per Brice Dudout, whose partial candidate readings are at bdudout.github.io/europe-chiffree/en/sega-1593.html. Tomokiyo, Cryptologia 43(1) 2019, gave a preliminary decipherment of 1593 continuous-figure texts, probably including no. 6. Not yet attempted or checked here.
why: The Curia's line on Henri IV's conversion and the Infanta's claim, and a report on the Suresnes conference, May 1593.
known: Nos. 6 and 8: Brice Dudout described both systems and gives partial candidate readings (bdudout.github.io); Tomokiyo (Cryptologia 43(1) 2019) gave a preliminary decipherment of 1593 figure texts, probably incl. no. 6. title: Catherine de' Medici to Paul de Foix, French ambassador in London, intercepted letter
correspondents: Catherine de' Medici → Paul de Foix (London)
status: Viewed 21 Sept 2026 (targets/foix1563/NOTES.md). The entry's two records were two different letters. R9238 (ff. 142-143, 'L'Amiral de France à la Reine d'Angleterre') is Coligny to Elizabeth, camp at Villefranche, 12 Jan 1563: deciphered at the time and calendared (CSP Foreign vi no. 76) and printed in Forbes, Full View ii; closed, and since 14 Oct 2026 part of targets/coligny1563/ (same Condé key R335). R9241's own letter (margin 'La Reine-mère de France à Mr de Foix Ambass. en Angleterre, 15 Jan 1563') is in neither Forbes nor CSP Foreign vi. About 950 tokens (Latin letters, digits, ligatures, a few two-digit numbers, clear nulls 'pour', 'car'), transcribed in targets/foix1563/qm_tokens.txt. Throckmorton's first, second and third ciphers and Croft's (R9260-R9262) do not fit, and homophonic annealing found no language (21 Sept). Since then the sign set was matched to Paul de Foix's own cipher, Tomokiyo's reconstruction from his 1565 letters (Feyseel Nur, PR #21), and Lawrence Beck's independent partial decipherment (PRs #18, #27) agrees with it on 19 of 25 shared signs: deciphered in part, below the read bar.
why: Catherine de' Medici writing in cipher to her ambassador in England during the first War of Religion, weeks after Dreux and while the English held Le Havre; the English intercepted it and Forbes's file kept the ciphertext, apparently with no decipherment.
known: R9238 (Coligny, 12 Jan 1563) deciphered at the time, in CSP Foreign vi and Forbes (coligny1563). R9241: key identified as Paul de Foix's own cipher, Tomokiyo's 1565 reconstruction (Feyseel Nur, PR #21); partial decipherment by Lawrence Beck (PRs #18, #27), converging with it (targets/foix1563, no page).
open: R9241 not at the read bar: 14 of 78 key entries rest on one occurrence, about a dozen signs (RX, monograms, numbers 10-82) unvalued, conflicts on 3, 2, z; needs a glyph audit on the images and a de Foix letter of 1563-64.
